column1: # *** WHAT IT SHOWS. *** Lerenas and Pelaezes at Trinidad married each other repeatedly across at
# least forty years, and by 1885 they were closely enough related that the church required a
# DISPENSATION FOR CONSANGUINITY to let them do it again - twice in the third degree, once in the
# second and third accumulated. These are not two families who happened to meet. They are one
# intermarried kindred in a small inland town.
# *** AND A NAME ECHOES ACROSS THEM. *** One of the six Trinidad Lerena fathers is VITALINO LERENA.
# The Pelaez groom dispensed in 1909 is VITALINO GREGORIO PELAES. A forename passing between two
# intermarried families is ordinary; it is recorded because it is one more thread tying them.
# *** WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW. *** Nothing here touches Pablo Armando. There is still no Pablo, no
# Armando and no Juan Carlos anywhere in the Trinidad set. This is a fact about the surname's
# founding kindred, not about his descent - and the dispensation register's own verdict stands:
# there is NO LERENA-LERENA DISPENSATION ANYWHERE, 1856-1932. Every Lerena in it marries out.
